title: The gospel of life (1995)
hookLine: John Paul II on the value of every human life

lines: I AM COME THAT THEY MAY HAVE LIFE.
cards: In John's Gospel, Jesus talks about sheep, a gate, and a thief. The thief, he says, comes only to steal and to kill and to destroy.
Then he gives the opposite reason for his own coming, in the Douay-Rheims: "I am come that they may have life, and may have it more abundantly." Not just kept alive. Abundantly.
John Paul the Second wrote a letter that sets life at the center of the gospel, and called it Evangelium Vitae. Today's word is its English name: the gospel of life.

teach.b: First, good news, not only a rule. The letter calls the gospel of life the heart of Jesus's message. Life is a gift to be welcomed and helped to grow, before it's a line to defend.
Second, an old question. The letter returns to Cain and Abel, where this block heard Cain's dodge.
It hears God's question, where is thy brother, asked again wherever a life is ended or treated as worthless, and the dodge coming back too: not my problem.
Then God's next words, in the Douay-Rheims: "the voice of thy brother's blood crieth to me from the earth." No life goes unheard. Every life has someone answerable for it.

Borrowing a list from the Second Vatican Council, the letter gathers many threats to life in one place: murder and genocide, abortion and euthanasia, and also subhuman living conditions, slavery, the selling of women and children, and disgraceful working conditions.
The Catholic Church teaches that directly and deliberately taking an innocent human life is always gravely wrong, and the letter applies that teaching to abortion and euthanasia.
It also keeps the poor, the sick, the old and the forgotten in the same frame. Fourth, a choice set before everyone.
This path heard Moses say it back in year two, in the Douay-Rheims: "Choose therefore life."
The letter speaks of building a culture of life: homes, hospitals, laws and habits where the weakest person in the room is safest.

how: Catholics live out the gospel of life through pregnancy and family support, hospice and care for the sick and elderly, outreach to the poor, and advocacy on laws affecting life, and parishes often pray for the protection of life at Mass.

games.q: what does “the gospel of life” mean?
o: the four Gospels' accounts of Jesus's life
a book of prayers for the sick and dying
John Paul II's letter on life as a gift

games.q: you're drawing up a list of threats to human life for a letter. what goes on it?
o: abortion and euthanasia, and nothing else.
war and violence, and nothing else.
a wide list, from murder and abortion to slavery and degrading work.
games.why: Evangelium Vitae borrows a wide list from the Second Vatican Council: murder, genocide, abortion, euthanasia, slavery, subhuman living conditions and disgraceful working conditions.

practice: Let God's question to Cain become yours: where is my brother, my sister?

Bring them to mind one at a time, without hurrying past any: a child not yet born and the mother carrying it, someone in a hospital bed tonight with no visitors, an old neighbor living alone, a person sleeping outside, a worker far away in a dangerous job.
If you pray, hold each one before God; if you don't, give each one a breath of real attention.

wordCard.voice: The gospel of life. John Paul the Second's letter, Evangelium Vitae: every human life a gift, and someone always answerable for it. Today's word.

orig.note: Latin: the gospel of life, the letter's opening words.

carryVoice: Your line: every life counts. Not just kept alive, but abundantly. Rest well.
